BiblicalUsage: This is the word for destruction itself — the place of ruin, the grave’s shadow. Job says ‘Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering’; Destruction and Death confess they have only heard a rumour of wisdom; and the proverb says ‘Hell and destruction are before the LORD’.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that destruction is never hidden from God — it is naked before Him, and even Death admits it does not hold wisdom. I believe that is the comfort under the dread: the pit has no secrets from the LORD, and nothing in it is beyond His sight or His reach.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
